text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.45% today, continuing a three-day slide that's wiped out 4.5% since October 20. The immediate driver appears to be a pullback in oil prices despite ongoing Middle East tensions—US crude dropped below $108 after hitting $116 earlier in the week, suggesting investors are digesting the geopolitical premium rather than pushing prices higher. When crude moves sharply lower, refiners' profit margins compress because they pay less for raw materials but the benefit doesn't always flow through immediately to their bottom line.

The broader context is that despite rising regional tensions and Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure, markets haven't sustained the panic-driven rally. US refineries are running at a healthy 93.4% utilization, and fuel storage levels remain ample, which removes any urgency-driven demand spike. The energy complex appears to be pricing in the conflict as a manageable risk rather than an imminent supply shock.
